per_file.paper_title: Discovery of Van Hove Singularities: Electronic Fingerprints of 3Q Magnetic Order in a van der Waals Quantum Magnet

expected_output.experiment_description: Single-crystal 2H-TaS2 and Co0.32TaS2 were cleaved and measured by low-temperature angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) at the Advanced Light Source MAESTRO beamline using a hemispherical electron analyzer. The pristine 2H-TaS2 sample was measured at T = 7 K with photon energy hν = 93 eV and linearly horizontal polarization. The Co0.32TaS2 sample was measured at T = 7 K with photon energy hν = 79 eV and linearly horizontal polarization on the TaS2-terminated surface. Fermi-surface maps and energy–momentum cuts were acquired along the M0–Γ0–K0 high-symmetry direction of the 2H-TaS2 Brillouin zone. Band dispersions were extracted by fitting Lorentzian peaks in momentum distribution curves and energy distribution curves. The comparison was used to quantify how Co intercalation modifies the TaS2-derived α and β bands and the spin-orbit-split momentum separation at the Fermi level.

alpha_band_minimum_shift_along_gamma0_k0.description: Measured binding-energy shift of the α-band minimum in Co0.32TaS2 relative to pristine 2H-TaS2 along the Γ0–K0 direction.

tas2_derived_band_bottom_shift_along_gam.description: Measured binding-energy shift of the TaS2-derived band bottom in Co0.32TaS2 relative to pristine 2H-TaS2 along the Γ0–M0 direction.

tas2_derived_band_shift_at_m0_meV.description: Measured binding-energy shift of the TaS2-derived band feature at M0 in Co0.32TaS2 relative to pristine 2H-TaS2.

spin_orbit_momentum_splitting_2h_tas2_in.description: Momentum splitting between the spin-orbit-split α and β bands at the Fermi level in pristine 2H-TaS2.

spin_orbit_momentum_splitting_co0_32tas2.description: Momentum splitting between the spin-orbit-split α and β bands at the Fermi level in Co0.32TaS2.

gamma_k_band_bottom_binding_energy_meV.description: Approximate binding energy of the shallow Co-derived γK electron-like band bottom near K in Co0.32TaS2.

gamma_m_band_top_binding_energy_meV.description: Approximate binding energy scale of the Co-derived γM hole-like feature near M in Co0.32TaS2.

expected_output.experiment_description: A Co-composition series of CoxTaS2 single crystals with x = 0.29, 0.31, 0.33, 0.34, and 0.36 was measured by ARPES at T = 7 K using photon energy hν = 79 eV and linearly horizontal polarization. Measurements were performed on TaS2-terminated surfaces. Energy–momentum spectra were acquired along the M0–Γ0–K0 high-symmetry direction, and energy distribution curves were taken at the M point. The α, β, γM, and γK band extrema were obtained from peak positions in fitted energy distribution curves, with γK extracted from spectra at the K point.

alpha_beta_band_downshift_x0_29_to_x0_36.description: Overall measured downward binding-energy shift of the TaS2-derived α and β bands when Co composition is increased from x = 0.29 to x = 0.36.

gamma_m_band_upturn_at_x0_36_meV.description: Small measured upward energy shift of the Co-derived γM band feature at x = 0.36 relative to its lower-composition trend.

gamma_k_band_upturn_at_x0_36_meV.description: Small measured upward energy shift of the Co-derived γK band feature at x = 0.36 relative to its lower-composition trend.

expected_output.experiment_description: A Co0.29TaS2 single crystal was measured by ARPES at T = 7 K using photon energy hν = 79 eV on a TaS2-terminated surface. The same cleaved surface was measured before and after successive in situ potassium depositions, with spectra acquired along the Γ0–K0 direction. Energy distribution curves at the M point were used to track the α, β, and γM band extrema as a function of potassium dosing.

gamma_m_band_shift_resolved_after_potass.description: Whether a resolvable shift of the Co-derived γM band was observed after potassium electron dosing of Co0.29TaS2.

alpha_beta_downshift_after_potassium_dos.description: Approximate downward shift of the TaS2-derived α and β bands after potassium dosing, described as comparable to the shift obtained by changing Co composition from x = 0.29 to x = 0.36.

expected_output.experiment_description: CoxTaS2 samples with Co compositions spanning x = 0.29 to 0.36 were measured by low-temperature ARPES at T = 7 K with photon energy hν = 79 eV. Fermi-surface maps were acquired around the Co-derived γ pockets in the Brillouin zone of the Co triangular superlattice. The triangular γ Fermi pockets were extracted from the raw Fermi-surface intensity maps and from momentum distribution curves along the K–M direction, allowing the Fermi-pocket topology to be compared across Co composition.

gamma_fermi_pocket_size_trend_with_co_co.description: Observed evolution of the Co-derived triangular γ Fermi pockets over the measured Co-composition series.

fermi_surface_topology_change_across_xc.description: Observed qualitative change in the γ-pocket Fermi-surface topology across the composition range near the reported critical composition.

expected_output.experiment_description: CoxTaS2 samples with Co compositions x = 0.29, 0.32, 0.33, 0.34, and 0.36 were measured by ARPES at T = 7 K with photon energy hν = 79 eV. Energy–momentum spectra were acquired along the K–M–K′ direction of the Co triangular-superlattice Brillouin zone. Second-derivative images with respect to energy and energy distribution curve stacks were used to determine the near-Fermi γ-band dispersion near the M point. Detailed raw spectra and EDCs were analyzed for x = 0.29 and x = 0.36 to compare the dispersion curvature and van Hove singularity structure.

gamma_band_vhs_count_x0_29.description: Number of van Hove singularity features inferred from the measured γ-band dispersion near M along K–M–K′ for Co0.29TaS2.

gamma_band_vhs_location_x0_29.description: Measured location of van Hove singularity features in the γ band near M for Co0.29TaS2.

per_file.paper_title: Device-independent quantum memory certification in two-point measurement experiments

expected_output.experiment_description: Device-independent two-point-measurement quantum-memory test on a trapped-ion processor. A chain of three ground-state-cooled 40Ca+ ions was confined in a macroscopic linear Paul trap. The two outer ions encoded qubits A′ and E, while the middle ion served only as a spacer to reduce optical cross-talk. Qubit manipulations used an individually addressed 729 nm quadrupole laser with linewidth below 1 Hz, incident at 67.5 degrees to the trap axis; single-ion addressing used a crossed acousto-optic-deflector setup. State readout used resonant 397 nm fluorescence collected onto an EMCCD camera. The two outer ions were initialized in a Bell state with a single Mølmer-Sørensen entangling gate. Qubit A′ was then measured at the first time point. A random variable X with alphabet {0,1,2,3} selected one of four Pauli measurements {+sigma_x,+sigma_z,-sigma_x,-sigma_z}; the binary first outcome was A. During this mid-circuit measurement, qubit E was spectroscopically decoupled by shelving it in unused D5/2 levels, followed by Doppler and polarization-gradient re-cooling. Qubit A was then re-prepared in a state depending only on A and not on X: the quantum-memory test used sigma_x eigenstates |+> and |-> as the two post-measurement states. A variable waiting time was inserted after the first measurement and before the two-qubit unitary; the displayed memory-decay experiment swept the wait time from 0 ms to 100 ms. Magnetic-field noise was mitigated with dynamical-decoupling echo pulses every 2.5 ms during the wait. The subsequent unitary consisted of a CNOT gate followed by a virtual full SWAP of the two qubit labels. The CNOT was implemented as R_C,0(pi/2) · R_T,pi(pi/2) · R_T,pi/4(pi) · MS_XX^{C,T}(pi/2) · R_T,pi/2(pi/2), where R_i,phi(theta) is a single-qubit equatorial rotation of qubit i by angle theta about phase phi, and MS_XX is a Mølmer-Sørensen XX interaction. The second-time binary measurement on qubit B was the observable (sigma_x+sigma_z)/sqrt(2). From the observed conditional probabilities Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x), the classicality parameter Gamma_Pr(AB|X) was computed as the sum over b0,b1 of the infimum over x of the sum over a of Pr(A=a,B=b_a|X=x). The same probability data were also used to evaluate Pearl’s cross-talk witness Delta_Pr(AB|X), defined as the maximum over a of the sum over b of the supremum over x of Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x). Cross-talk was additionally addressed by estimating the average causal direct effect ACDE, the supremum over a,b,x,x′ of the absolute difference between Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x)=b) and Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x′)=b). The qubit-memory fidelity lower bound was inferred from Gamma_Pr(AB|X) using the paper’s device-independent qubit-memory bound.

temporal_correlation_gamma.description: Measured value of the two-point-measurement classicality parameter Gamma_Pr(AB|X) for the optimized quantum-memory certification sequence with no added storage delay beyond the base sequence; classical memory models obey Gamma_Pr(AB|X) >= 1.

qubit_memory_fidelity_lower_bound_percen.description: Device-independent lower bound, in percent, on the fidelity of the implemented qubit memory channel to an ideal qubit memory channel inferred from the measured temporal correlations.

pearl_cross_talk_parameter.description: Measured Pearl-inequality parameter Delta_Pr(AB|X) obtained from the same optimized quantum-memory data; values above 1 would witness cross-talk influence.

average_causal_direct_effect.description: Measured average causal direct effect used to quantify direct cross-talk influence from the first measurement setting X to the second outcome B not mediated by A.

certified_quantum_memory_time_ms.description: Storage time over which the trapped-ion qubit memory was reported to be certified as quantum by the temporal-correlation protocol.

expected_output.experiment_description: Two-point-measurement experiment testing non-classical quantum causal relations with a partial-swap interaction on the same three-ion 40Ca+ trapped-ion processor. The outer ions encoded qubits A′ and E and were initialized in a Bell state using a single Mølmer-Sørensen gate; the middle ion acted as a spacer. Individual control used the addressed 729 nm laser at 67.5 degrees to the trap axis, and fluorescence readout used 397 nm light and an EMCCD camera. At the first time point, qubit A′ was measured with X in {0,1,2,3} selecting the four Pauli observables {+sigma_x,+sigma_z,-sigma_x,-sigma_z}, yielding binary outcome A. Qubit E was shelved during the mid-circuit measurement to suppress measurement back-action, and the ion chain was re-cooled afterward. The post-measurement qubit A was prepared in a sigma_y eigenstate depending only on A and not on X: |+i> for one binary outcome and |-i> for the other, according to the paper’s post-processing convention. The two-qubit interaction was the partial-swap gate U_PS(alpha)=cos(alpha/2) id + i sin(alpha/2) U_swap, where alpha is the controlled swap angle in radians, id is the two-qubit identity, and U_swap is the full two-qubit swap operator. The experiment swept alpha from 0 to pi. In the trapped-ion circuit, U_PS(alpha) was implemented as MS_ZZ(-alpha/2) · MS_YY(-alpha/2) · MS_XX(-alpha/2), with the Mølmer-Sørensen rotation angle controlled through laser intensity while keeping gate time fixed. The second-time measurement on qubit B was sigma_x. For each alpha, the same temporal-correlation classicality parameter Gamma_Pr(AB|X) was evaluated from Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x), and violation of the classical causal bound was used to certify non-classical causal relations.

alpha_interval_with_observed_nonclassica.description: Swap-angle interval, in radians, over which the partial-swap two-point-measurement experiment exhibited violations of the classical causal inequality, thereby certifying non-classical causal relations.

expected_output.experiment_description: Noise and coherence characterization of the trapped-ion qubit memory used to model the decay of the two-point-measurement memory-certification signal. The same 40Ca+ trapped-ion processor was operated with qubit manipulation by the addressed 729 nm laser and readout by 397 nm fluorescence. Coherent magnetic-field noise at the 50 Hz mains frequency was actively compensated, while a remaining 100 Hz component was mitigated by dynamical decoupling. The experiment applied echo pulses at 2.5 ms intervals during variable waiting periods. Ramsey experiments were performed over a waiting-time sweep from 0 ms to 200 ms; the Ramsey contrast was measured as a function of waiting time and fitted with an exponential decay model to obtain the effective dephasing time T2 under the applied dynamical-decoupling sequence. The same echo pulse used in the memory sequence was also calibrated to estimate its average pulse fidelity.

effective_coherence_time_t2_ms.description: Effective dephasing time T2 of the trapped-ion qubit under the dynamical-decoupling sequence, obtained from an exponential fit to Ramsey-contrast decay.

single_echo_pulse_average_fidelity.description: Average fidelity of an individual echo pulse used in the dynamical-decoupling sequence for the memory-decay experiment.

report_experiments.experiment_description: Device-independent two-point-measurement quantum-memory test on a trapped-ion processor. A chain of three ground-state-cooled 40Ca+ ions was confined in a macroscopic linear Paul trap. The two outer ions encoded qubits A′ and E, while the middle ion served only as a spacer to reduce optical cross-talk. Qubit manipulations used an individually addressed 729 nm quadrupole laser with linewidth below 1 Hz, incident at 67.5 degrees to the trap axis; single-ion addressing used a crossed acousto-optic-deflector setup. State readout used resonant 397 nm fluorescence collected onto an EMCCD camera. The two outer ions were initialized in a Bell state with a single Mølmer-Sørensen entangling gate. Qubit A′ was then measured at the first time point. A random variable X with alphabet {0,1,2,3} selected one of four Pauli measurements {+sigma_x,+sigma_z,-sigma_x,-sigma_z}; the binary first outcome was A. During this mid-circuit measurement, qubit E was spectroscopically decoupled by shelving it in unused D5/2 levels, followed by Doppler and polarization-gradient re-cooling. Qubit A was then re-prepared in a state depending only on A and not on X: the quantum-memory test used sigma_x eigenstates |+> and |-> as the two post-measurement states. A variable waiting time was inserted after the first measurement and before the two-qubit unitary; the displayed memory-decay experiment swept the wait time from 0 ms to 100 ms. Magnetic-field noise was mitigated with dynamical-decoupling echo pulses every 2.5 ms during the wait. The subsequent unitary consisted of a CNOT gate followed by a virtual full SWAP of the two qubit labels. The CNOT was implemented as R_C,0(pi/2) · R_T,pi(pi/2) · R_T,pi/4(pi) · MS_XX^{C,T}(pi/2) · R_T,pi/2(pi/2), where R_i,phi(theta) is a single-qubit equatorial rotation of qubit i by angle theta about phase phi, and MS_XX is a Mølmer-Sørensen XX interaction. The second-time binary measurement on qubit B was the observable (sigma_x+sigma_z)/sqrt(2). From the observed conditional probabilities Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x), the classicality parameter Gamma_Pr(AB|X) was computed as the sum over b0,b1 of the infimum over x of the sum over a of Pr(A=a,B=b_a|X=x). The same probability data were also used to evaluate Pearl’s cross-talk witness Delta_Pr(AB|X), defined as the maximum over a of the sum over b of the supremum over x of Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x). Cross-talk was additionally addressed by estimating the average causal direct effect ACDE, the supremum over a,b,x,x′ of the absolute difference between Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x)=b) and Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x′)=b). The qubit-memory fidelity lower bound was inferred from Gamma_Pr(AB|X) using the paper’s device-independent qubit-memory bound.

Measured average causal direct effect used to quantify direct cross-talk influence from the first measurement setting X to the second outcome B not mediated by A.
Storage time over which the trapped-ion qubit memory was reported to be certified as quantum by the temporal-correlation protocol.
